## python script to keep only the longest isoform of a gene. If there are multiple isoforms of the same size, it keeps the first occurance

### to run this use the bash script "remove_duplicates.sh"

```{python, eval=FALSE}
from Bio import SeqIO
import sys
import re

lastGene = None
longest = (None, None)

def extract_gene_name(description):
    # 1.Format 1: ENSGALT...#GENENAME#...
    hash_match = re.search(r'#([^#|]+)#', description)
    if hash_match:
        return hash_match.group(1)

    # 2.Format 2: [gene=...]
    gene_match = re.search(r'\[gene=([^\]]+)\]', description)
    if gene_match:
        return gene_match.group(1)

    # 3.Use the whole ID if no pattern matches
    return description.split()[0]

for rec in SeqIO.parse(sys.argv[1], "fasta"):
    gene = extract_gene_name(rec.description)
    l = len(rec)

    if lastGene is not None:
        if gene == lastGene:
            if longest[0] < l:
                longest = (l, rec)
        else:
            SeqIO.write(longest[1], sys.stdout, "fasta")
            lastGene = gene
            longest = (l, rec)
    else:
        lastGene = gene
        longest = (l, rec)

# Write the final accumulated sequence
if longest[1] is not None:
    SeqIO.write(longest[1], sys.stdout, "fasta")

```
